To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the media do indeed have an impact on the public's understanding of the environment.
1) the media is a key source of environmental information, 2) the media is not a neutral source, and 3) there are important differences between different media.

(1) the mass media have an important role to play in the communication of environmental information; (2) the mass media do play a significant role in the communication of such information to the UK population, although the extent and nature of this role varies across different media; (3) there is no single, simple relationship between the mass media and the public; and (4) the mass media can be a useful source of information for environmental decision-making.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how the mass media, in particular, television and radio, can contribute to the public’s environmental awareness, understanding and concern.

the ways in which the media construct and present environmental issues to the public, and how these constructions and presentations influence public understanding of, and engagement in, the environment.
how the media, and particularly the news media, represent environmental information to the public.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the media is a powerful influence in the way that people perceive the environment.
the media are a significant source of information about environmental issues, but they do not appear to influence the public’s attitudes or behaviour in the ways that some commentators would suggest.
the media do not have an overall negative or positive impact on the environment and the public.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the media is not the message, but the medium through which the message is conveyed.
media representations have a strong influence on public perceptions, attitudes and beliefs about environmental issues.
the mass media are not the only source of public knowledge about the environment, and they are not the most important source either.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the media is an effective way of reaching the public and that the public is willing to learn from the media about environmental issues.
media coverage of climate change is not just important for the public's knowledge of climate change, but also for its attitudes and behaviors.
the media are an important part of the public's environmental information diet.
